findings.issue_text: [BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil for any database where the 'embed_category' site_settings row does not exist. Discourse stores only non-default site settings in the site_settings table, so on any install that never changed embed_category the SELECT returns zero rows, `[0]` is nil, and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError — the deploy's `rake db:migrate` aborts and the app cannot boot against the migrated schema. Fresh installs are guaranteed to hit this.

[BUG] `this.store.createRecord('embeddable-host')` references a model type that is never defined anywhere in the codebase — no model file for 'embeddable-host' (or 'embedding') exists in this diff or is referenced as pre-existing. The Discourse store resolves model types via container lookup of `model:embeddable-host`; with no such factory registered, `createRecord` fails and the 'Add Host' button in the admin embedding screen throws instead of adding a row — the feature's primary creation flow cannot work as shipped.

[BUG] The `update` action calls `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally dereferences the result in `save_host`, which does `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` on a nil `host` object and `host.category_id =`. A PUT to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale or nonexistent id (two admins, one deletes a host while the other has the edit row open) returns a 500 NoMethodError instead of a 404; the same unchecked pattern exists in `destroy` (line 20-22) where `host.destroy` on nil raises.

[ADVISORY] The `update` action re-serializes the fetched embedding without applying any changes — it is a silent no-op that still returns 200. The admin-embedding controller's `saveChanges` action fires `embedding.update({})` against this endpoint; any future embedding-level fields edited in the UI are silently discarded while the admin sees a successful save, and no code path exists to persist anything through PUT /admin/customize/embedding.

[ADVISORY] Host values migrated from the old embeddable_hosts setting are interpolated directly into a hand-written SQL INSERT with single quotes and no escaping. Any legacy embeddable_hosts value containing an apostrophe or backslash (a hostname-adjacent entry like `eviltrout's.com`, which the old free-text setting accepted) makes the migration raise a SQL syntax error, blocking the upgrade for that site; values with an http:// prefix are also inserted untrimmed, unlike what the model's before_validation would produce.

[ADVISORY] The new plural-id hydration branch calls `self.pluralize(subType)`, but the pluralization target name is never coordinated with the model/adapter naming that the rest of the pipeline uses (`embeddable_host` ids hydrate into a `pluralize`-derived key while the consuming template iterates `embedding.embeddable_hosts`). If `store.pluralize` does not produce exactly 'embeddable_hosts' for 'embeddable_host' (or does not exist as a method on this store), the hydrated list lands on a mismatched key and the admin embedding table renders empty even though the API returned hosts; this coupling is only exercised by the fruit/color test fixtures, not by any embedding-endpoint test.

[ADVISORY] The diff empties category_fabricator.rb of all category fabricators and moves them into embeddable_host_fabricator.rb, leaving the category fabricator file containing a single embeddable_host definition. Any future contributor looking for or adding a category fabricator edits the wrong file, and the odd file/name inversion (embeddable_host defined in category_fabricator.rb, categories defined in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb) makes every subsequent fabricator change slower and more error-prone to locate.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on any install where no site_settings row named 'embed_category' exists (fresh installs, sites that never touched embedding), because execute(...)[0] returns nil and ['id'] is called on it. `rake db:migrate` raises NoMethodError (undefined method `[]' for nil:NilClass) on every fresh install, blocking deploys entirely.

[BUG] The INSERT statement interpolates the raw host string '#{h}' from the old embeddable_hosts setting without SQL escaping, so any value containing a single quote breaks the migration and permits SQL injection via a stored setting value. Any existing embeddable_hosts entry with an apostrophe or quote aborts db:migrate mid-migration with a PG syntax error, leaving a half-created table and half-deleted site settings.

[BUG] The update action renders the serializer but never saves anything, so the frontend 'saveChanges' button at admin-embedding.js.es6 (which calls embedding.update({})) is a silent no-op that discards user input. An admin who hits save on the embedding screen gets a success response while nothing is persisted — data loss with no error surfaced.

[BUG] update calls EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and passes the result to save_host without a nil check, so a nonexistent or stale id raises NoMethodError on nil.host= and returns a 500 instead of a 404. Any update request for a deleted host id (e.g. two admins editing concurrently, one deletes) crashes with a 500. destroy at line 19 has the same nil.destroy 500.

[ADVISORY] The controller specs for both new controllers assert only superclass ancestry and never exercise create/update/destroy, so the entire host CRUD behavior this feature adds (including the nil-id 500 above, blank-host validation, category fallback) is untested. A regression in host saving/validation ships green; the only model-level tests cover string trimming and host_allowed?, not the controller contract.

[ADVISORY] The category fabricators were moved into spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb while category_fabricator.rb was repurposed to hold the embeddable_host fabricator, so every Fabricate(:category) call site now resolves its fabricator from a file named embeddable_host_fabricator.rb. The next contributor adding a category fabricator edits category_fabricator.rb (now a misleadingly-named file) or duplicates definitions; both files' contents contradict their filenames, making the test suite harder to navigate safely.

[ADVISORY] The host validation regex caps the TLD at 5 letters (\.[a-z]{2,5}) and rejects valid inputs like 'example.travel' or 'example.museum', and the model has no uniqueness constraint on host. An admin saving a host on a long-TLD domain gets a validation error on a legitimate host, and duplicate rows for the same host can be created since neither model validation nor the migration enforces uniqueness.

[BUG] The embed_category lookup crashes the migration with NoMethodError on any site where the embed_category site setting row was never created. `execute(...WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'`)[0]` is nil when no row exists (setting never customized), so `[0]['id']` raises NoMethodError and the entire deploy-time migration fails, blocking upgrades for every forum that never set embed_category.

[BUG] The host insert interpolates the raw setting value into SQL unescaped. Any existing embeddable_hosts line containing an apostrophe (e.g. `o'brien.example.com`) produces broken SQL and the migration aborts mid-way, having already deleted nothing but having created a partially-populated table; use quote/parameterized inserts.

[BUG] The migration permanently deletes the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings inside an irreversible `change` migration with no down path and no data preserved anywhere else. If the deploy is rolled back, all embeddable-host configuration is permanently lost — operators cannot recover the prior allowlist; the data deletion is also baked into schema change making `db:migrate:rollback` fail or silently drop data.

[BUG] The `update` action is a no-op: it re-serializes the fetched OpenStruct without applying any params, so PUT /admin/customize/embedding silently discards whatever the client sends. The controller declares a mutation endpoint in the PR title's feature ('can edit embedding') that accepts a PUT, returns 200 with success-shaped JSON, and persists nothing — any client exercising it (including the controller's own `saveChanges` action in admin-embedding.js.es6) gets silent data loss of its payload.

[ADVISORY] The `saveChanges` action calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` with an empty payload and nothing in the diff's templates ever invokes it. Dead code shipped as part of the feature: the next maintainer editing the embedding settings screen will assume a save path exists when the only reachable behavior is a no-op server round-trip; either wire it to real state or delete it.

[ADVISORY] The PR rewrites the generic `_hydrateEmbedded` store hydration (plural `_ids` support) — a framework-wide change to every model hydrating `*_ids` keys — justified only by the embedding serializer's `embed: :ids`. Any other REST payload that happens to carry a `foo_ids` key now has it consumed and deleted from the raw object where previously it passed through untouched; the change is verified only by fruit fixtures in the test pretender, so a regression in a non-embedding consumer of the store would ship unnoticed. The blast radius (all models) exceeds what the 'edit category/host relationships' requirement needs.

[ADVISORY] Removing the `embed_category` site setting replaces a global default category with per-host category, but when `record_for_host(url)` returns false (no matching host), `eh.try(:category_id)` is nil and the topic lands in uncategorized with no fallback or warning. Operators who previously relied on embed_category for feed-polled topics from URLs whose host isn't in the table (TopicRetriever checks the host, but any path where import runs without a host record) silently get topics in uncategorized instead of their configured category — a silent behavior regression not required by 'edit category/host relationships'.

[ADVISORY] The diff gutted category_fabricator.rb down to only the embeddable_host fabricator and moved all category fabricators into a new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb file. Category fabricators now live in a file named after an unrelated model; the next contributor adding a category fabricator will edit the wrong file or duplicate definitions, and the file move is untraceable to any requirement in this feature — it should have stayed in category_fabricator.rb with the new host fabricator in its own file.

[BUG] The backfill inserts raw site-setting values via raw SQL, bypassing EmbeddableHost's before_validation normalization, so migrated hosts keep 'http://' prefixes, paths, and mixed case while every later lookup strips them. A site upgrading with embeddable_hosts='http://discourse.org\nhttps://example.com/1234' (a documented valid format — the old tests used exactly this) gets rows stored as 'http://discourse.org', and EmbeddableHost.record_for_host's where("lower(host) = ?", uri.host) never matches, so embedding 403s for all pre-existing hosts after upgrade with no error surfaced.

[ADVISORY] The hot-path lookup uses non-sargable where("lower(host) = ?", ...) with no index on embeddable_hosts.host created anywhere in the migration. Every embedded-comments request (embed_controller#ensure_embeddable) and every TopicRetriever call runs a full-table-scan lower() comparison; with thousands of hosts or on a busy embed traffic site this becomes a per-request linear scan the schema never anticipated.

[BUG] The lookup lowercases the stored column but not the probe: where("lower(host) = ?", host) compares against the raw uri.host, which Ruby's URI does not downcase. A referer header like 'http://EvilTrout.com/page' yields uri.host='EvilTrout.com' which never matches even a correctly-stored 'eviltrout.com' row, so legitimate embeds from mixed-case hosts are rejected with InvalidAccess; meanwhile the model's before_validation never downcases saved values, so the asymmetry is one-sided in the wrong direction.

[BUG] update and destroy call EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first with no not-found handling, then immediately invoke save_host(host) / host.destroy on nil. A PUT or DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale id (host deleted in another tab, or a double-click racing the destroy) raises NoMethodError on nil, returning a 500 instead of the 404 the REST adapter expects.

[ADVISORY] The embeddable_hosts table has no UNIQUE constraint on host and no FK on category_id, so the schema cannot enforce the real business invariant that a host is allowed once. Two admins (or the save-vs-create race — create always builds EmbeddableHost.new rather than checking for an existing row) can insert duplicate host rows; record_for_host then matches an arbitrary one, and its category_id becomes dependent on insertion order.

[ADVISORY] The PUT /admin/customize/embedding route exists and the client saveChanges() calls this.get('embedding').update({}), but the controller's update action performs no update — it just re-serializes the unchanged OpenStruct. The advertised write endpoint is a silent no-op: any caller that PUTs embedding settings gets a 200 success while nothing is persisted, a stand-in guard for 'saving embedding settings' that can go green while nothing was saved.

[BUG] expandable_first_post? silently drops the 'embeddable hosts configured' gate that was part of the accepted behavior, changing the condition from 'hosts set AND truncate AND embedded' to just 'truncate AND embedded'. On any forum where embed_truncate is enabled but no embeddable hosts exist, embedded-style topics with topic_embeds render with the expandable first post, a behavior the old site-settings contract explicitly prevented; this objective change was made as a side effect of the settings migration with no evidence of explicit acceptance.

[BUG] The EmbeddingController#update action persists nothing — it re-fetches and re-serializes, and the client's saveChanges calls embedding.update({}) with an empty payload, so the admin 'Embedding' settings save button is a silent no-op. Admins clicking save on the embedding screen see a success response while nothing is written; the PR title promises editing category/host relationships, and host editing works only via the separate embeddable_hosts endpoints, but any future settings placed on this form are silently discarded.

[ADVISORY] category_fabricator.rb was gutted and now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the category fabricators were moved wholesale into a new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — the fabricator definitions and their filenames now contradict each other in both files. The next developer running `grep category_fabricator` or adding a category fabricator will edit the wrong file or duplicate definitions; this appears to be a review-iteration artifact (an accidental file swap) rather than a deliberate restructuring, since :diff_category/:happy_category/:private_category now live in a file named embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

[ADVISORY] The migration irreversibly DELETEs the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings rows after copying them, with no down path that restores them, so the old configuration is permanently destroyed on migration. Operators who need to roll back this deploy lose their configured hosts entirely (down only drops the table); the data migration should preserve the source settings until the feature is confirmed stable.

[BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when no site_settings row named 'embed_category' exists, because `execute(...)[0]['id']` indexes into an empty result array before the category_id == 0 fallback is checked. Fresh installs or any database without a seeded embed_category row abort the migration mid-transaction; the null-check is placed after the dereference that can raise.

[ADVISORY] Migrated host strings are interpolated directly into a raw INSERT statement without escaping, so a host value containing a single quote (accepted by the old free-text site setting) breaks or corrupts the migration. Forums whose legacy embeddable_hosts setting contains e.g. `o'brien.example.com` hit a SQL syntax error during deploy; the new model validation would reject such hosts, but the migration runs before any validation can clean them.

[ADVISORY] The _hydrateEmbedded change broadens a shared, load-bearing store primitive (singular *_id handling) to also rewrite plural *_ids keys to a pluralized type, a change to core serialization hydration semantics made in service of the embedding feature. Any existing API whose payload coincidentally contains a `*_ids` key now gets those keys deleted and replaced with a hydrated `pluralize(subType)` array; if the subType is not a registered model, _lookupSubType returns undefined and the ids array is silently replaced by [undefined], corrupting consumers of any payload field ending in _ids — this is a silent public-surface change to the store affecting all Ember clients, not just embedding.

[BUG] The migration string-interpolates former embeddable_hosts setting values directly into INSERT statements. execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)" — a value in the legacy embeddable_hosts site setting containing a single quote breaks out of the string literal and injects arbitrary SQL into the migration run, which executes with full DDL privileges; a malicious or merely quote-containing host value corrupts or drops data during deploy.

[BUG] update and destroy look up EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then call methods on the result without checking for nil, producing an unhandled NoMethodError when the id does not exist. A staff user (or any stale admin UI with a deleted host row) submitting a nonexistent id gets a 500 error with a stack trace in production logs instead of a 404, and host.update/destroy never completes — the delete confirmation flow hangs on the client for already-removed hosts.

[ADVISORY] The update action never reads or persists any params, so the admin Embedding page's save action is a silent no-op that still returns a success response. An admin who clicks save on the embedding settings believes changes were saved (200 OK, re-serialized current state) when nothing was written — any future settings added to this UI will silently fail to persist until the action is implemented, and there is currently no server-side code path that writes Embedding-level settings at all.

[ADVISORY] The controller gates mutation of the embed allowlist with ensure_staff rather than requiring an admin, despite every sibling admin controller inheriting AdminController's admin check semantics via routes constrained by AdminConstraint. On any deployment where staff members are not trusted with security settings, a moderator-class user can add an arbitrary host to the embed allowlist (letting their own site embed forum comments and create topics via TopicEmbed.import with cook_method raw_html), broadening the trust boundary the X-Frame-Options/ALLOWALL embed surface depends on.

[BUG] The 'find embedded' test asserts fruit 2's colors but the pretender handler for /fruits/:id ignores the requested id and always returns fruits[0] (apple, color_ids [1,2]), so the test validates the mock's wrong-record response, not per-id hydration. The assertion fruitCols.length === 2 passes only because the fixture handler is broken; if the handler were corrected to return fruit 2 (color_ids [3]), this test would fail — meaning the suite currently locks in the broken handler and would mask a real hydration regression for non-first records. Checked: test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6 and test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6.

[BUG] The test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what its name claims: the diff removed the embeddable_hosts presence check from expandable_first_post?, and this test now passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false in that context — the blank-host condition contributes nothing. The behavior change in this diff (expandable_first_post? returning true when no hosts exist but embed_truncate and topic_embed are set) has no test that exercises it; a reader of the suite believes the blank-host guard still exists and a regression restoring/removing the check would go undetected. Checked: spec/models/topic_spec.rb — no test covers the no-hosts-with-truncate-true case.

[ADVISORY] The only test for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts the class's superclass — an inheritance check that cannot fail while any controller behavior is broken. create/update/destroy, the category_id-blank fallback to uncategorized_category_id, and render_json_error on validation failure are entirely unverified; a regression in save_host (e.g. nil host from params crashing with NoMethodError) ships green. Checked: this is the only spec file referencing EmbeddableHostsController in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The only test for Admin::EmbeddingController asserts superclass inheritance, so no controller behavior is exercised. The show action's serialization of embedding with embedded host ids and the fetch_embedding ordering (EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)) are unverified; an N+1/ordering/serialization regression ships undetected. Checked: this is the only spec file referencing EmbeddingController in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The model spec tests only the trimming happy path of the host format validation; no test exercises a host that fails the regex (e.g. 'not a host', 'eviltrout', empty), so the validation branch is unverifiable from the suite. A loosened or broken regex in EmbeddableHost's validates_format_of (e.g. an edit that accepts any string) passes all specs, letting admins save invalid hosts that then silently fail host_allowed? matching in production embeds. Checked: spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb is the only spec for this model.

[ADVISORY] The migration's data-migration logic (site_settings to embeddable_hosts row copying, category_id fallback, SQL string interpolation) has no spec coverage anywhere in the diff. The first row of the execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories INNER JOIN site_settings...") will raise NoMethodError for nil ([]) on any site where embed_category was never set — the [0]['id'].to_i call on an empty result — and this crash-on-migrate path is never exercised, so a fresh install or a site without embed settings blocks on db:migrate. Checked: no spec file in the diff references this migration or EmbeddableHost data migration.

[BUG] The data migration guard is a dead guard: `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` is always 0 for a SELECT under PostgreSQL, so the INSERT loop never runs while the paired DELETE is unconditional. On any site with existing embeddable_hosts configured, the migration deletes the site_settings rows for embeddable_hosts and embed_category without creating any EmbeddableHost records — every existing embed host is silently lost, embeds stop working, and there is no backup or rollback path.

[BUG] The category lookup crashes with NoMethodError when the embed_category site setting row is absent or its value matches no category name. `execute(...)` returns an empty result set, so `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError — the migration aborts mid-run on every site that never set embed_category (the vast majority, since its default is ''), leaving the deploy broken and schema_migrations inconsistent.

[BUG] `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` makes this migration destructive on re-run. If the migration ever re-executes against an environment where the table exists and holds data (restore-from-backup, bin/rake db:migrate against a partially-migrated snapshot), force: true drops the table and destroys all embeddable host rows with no confirmation.

[BUG] Host values from the old setting are interpolated directly into the INSERT SQL without escaping or parameterization. Any legacy host value containing a single quote (a user could save e.g. `o'brien.com` via the old host_list setting) breaks the INSERT with a syntax error, aborting the migration before the setting rows are migrated — and the data-integrity layer's validation (the model strips schemes/paths and validates format) is bypassed entirely, so junk rows land in the table unvalidated.

[BUG] The migration is irreversible: it DELETEs the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site_settings rows with no down method or export to restore them. Once applied, rolling back discards the original configuration permanently — there is no path to reconstruct the old setting values, so any operator needing to revert this deploy loses their embed configuration.

[ADVISORY] The fallback to uncategorized_category_id only covers category_id == 0, but a missing/blank embed_category crashes earlier at the lookup, so the fallback is unreachable in the most common case. Operators who intentionally left embed_category blank (expecting uncategorized posts) hit a failed migration instead of the graceful fallback the code clearly intends.

[BUG] update and destroy call save_host/destroy on a nil host when params[:id] does not match any EmbeddableHost, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 where the admin API contract implies a 404. `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` is nil; `host.host = ...` (line 27) or `host.destroy` (line 19) raises NoMethodError, producing a raw 500 with a stack trace in the admin log instead of a 4xx error payload the frontend's popupAjaxError can render.

[BUG] save_host raises NoMethodError with a 500 when the embeddable_host param envelope is missing (params[:embeddable_host] is nil), instead of a 400-style validation error. A request to POST /admin/embeddable_hosts without an embeddable_host key crashes on `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` before validation ever runs; the admin sees a generic 500 rather than the render_json_error path the endpoint was built to serve.

[BUG] The delete flow calls destroyRecord().then(...) with no .catch, so a failed DELETE leaves the promise rejection unhandled and the admin gets no error while the row stays in the list with stale state. If the server rejects the destroy (e.g. a 500 or network failure), no popupAjaxError fires, the row remains in the table as if delete silently did nothing, and an unhandled rejection is logged; contrast with save() which does catch popupAjaxError — the delete path has zero error surfacing.

[ADVISORY] The update action performs no persistence whatsoever — it re-fetches and re-serializes the unchanged OpenStruct — so PUT /admin/customize/embedding returns a success response while saving nothing. The frontend's saveChanges() calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` with no error handling; any admin invocation of the embedding save flow silently no-ops with a 200, leaving the user believing their settings were saved.

[ADVISORY] saveChanges fires embedding.update({}) with no .then/.catch and no in-flight guard, so overlapping invocations interleave and failures are silently swallowed. An admin whose update request fails (network drop, 4xx) never sees any error or retry state — the request's rejection is entirely unobserved and the UI stays in its pre-save state with no indication anything failed.

[BUG] The before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! on a nil host, raising NoMethodError before validation can report the empty-host error. Any code path that builds/saves an EmbeddableHost with host unset (nil rather than empty string) crashes with NoMethodError in the callback; the model's own presence/format validation for a missing host never gets the chance to produce a 4xx error, so the failure surfaces as a 500.

goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

matched_golden_ids: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core bug: the query uses lower(host) but passes an un-normalized (potentially mixed-case) host parameter, so case-insensitive matching fails for mixed-case referer/URI hosts. Extra notes about validation don’t change that it matches the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update and destroy call EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first with no not-found handling, then immediately invoke save_host(host) / host.destroy on nil. A PUT or DELETE to /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id with a stale id (host deleted in another tab, or a double-click racing the destroy) raises NoMethodError on nil, returning a 500 instead of the 404 the REST adapter expects.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the code fetches with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and does not handle the case where no record is found. `update` then calls `save_host(host)` which immediately dereferences `host` (`host.host = ...`), and `destroy` calls `host.destroy`; both will raise `NoMethodError` if `host` is `nil`, yielding a 500 on stale/invalid ids.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The embeddable_hosts table has no UNIQUE constraint on host and no FK on category_id, so the schema cannot enforce the real business invariant that a host is allowed once. Two admins (or the save-vs-create race — create always builds EmbeddableHost.new rather than checking for an existing row) can insert duplicate host rows; record_for_host then matches an arbitrary one, and its category_id becomes dependent on insertion order.

adjudication.rationale: In the migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` the table is created with `t.string :host` and `t.integer :category_id` but no unique index/constraint on `host` and no FK on `category_id` (diff shows none added). The admin create path always does `save_host(EmbeddableHost.new)` (Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#create) and there is no model-level `validates_uniqueness_of :host`, so concurrent admins or repeated creates can insert duplicate `host` rows. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` then does `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, making the chosen row (and thus category used in `TopicEmbed.import` via `eh.try(:category_id)`) dependent on insertion order/arbitrary DB ordering when duplicates exist.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PUT /admin/customize/embedding route exists and the client saveChanges() calls this.get('embedding').update({}), but the controller's update action performs no update — it just re-serializes the unchanged OpenStruct. The advertised write endpoint is a silent no-op: any caller that PUTs embedding settings gets a 200 success while nothing is persisted, a stand-in guard for 'saving embedding settings' that can go green while nothing was saved.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a PUT route `put "customize/embedding" => "embedding#update"` and a client action `saveChanges()` that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})`. However, `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` ignores any params and simply `render_serialized(@embedding, ...)`, where `@embedding` is a freshly built `OpenStruct` in `fetch_embedding` (id + `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`). No data is written or persisted, so the PUT endpoint is a silent no-op that returns success while saving nothing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] expandable_first_post? silently drops the 'embeddable hosts configured' gate that was part of the accepted behavior, changing the condition from 'hosts set AND truncate AND embedded' to just 'truncate AND embedded'. On any forum where embed_truncate is enabled but no embeddable hosts exist, embedded-style topics with topic_embeds render with the expandable first post, a behavior the old site-settings contract explicitly prevented; this objective change was made as a side effect of the settings migration with no evidence of explicit acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Topic#expandable_first_post?` from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to only `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb). The `embeddable_hosts` site setting is removed, but there is no replacement gate such as checking `EmbeddableHost` records. Therefore, if `embed_truncate` is enabled and a topic has an existing `topic_embed`, `expandable_first_post?` will now return true even when there are zero allowed embeddable hosts configured—behavior that was previously prevented by the `embeddable_hosts.present?` condition. The updated spec no longer asserts this gate (spec/models/topic_spec.rb), so the regression is not caught.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The EmbeddingController#update action persists nothing — it re-fetches and re-serializes, and the client's saveChanges calls embedding.update({}) with an empty payload, so the admin 'Embedding' settings save button is a silent no-op. Admins clicking save on the embedding screen see a success response while nothing is written; the PR title promises editing category/host relationships, and host editing works only via the separate embeddable_hosts endpoints, but any future settings placed on this form are silently discarded.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` does not persist anything (it just re-serializes `@embedding`), and the Ember controller’s `saveChanges()` calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` with an empty payload. However, the provided admin template (`admin/templates/embedding.hbs`) contains no “save” button or any invocation of `saveChanges`, and host/category edits are actually persisted via the separate `embeddable-host` component calling `host.save(...)` against the `/admin/embeddable_hosts` endpoints. So the core observation is grounded (the update endpoint is a no-op), but the claimed user-visible “save button is a silent no-op” is not evidenced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] category_fabricator.rb was gutted and now defines Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the category fabricators were moved wholesale into a new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb — the fabricator definitions and their filenames now contradict each other in both files. The next developer running `grep category_fabricator` or adding a category fabricator will edit the wrong file or duplicate definitions; this appears to be a review-iteration artifact (an accidental file swap) rather than a deliberate restructuring, since :diff_category/:happy_category/:private_category now live in a file named embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` no longer defines `Fabricator(:category)` and instead now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the new file `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` fabricators. This filename/content swap is real and will confuse future maintenance (e.g., developers searching for category fabricators will look in the wrong file). However, it likely won’t break runtime/test behavior since Fabricator definitions are loaded regardless of filename, so it’s more of a correctness-of-structure/maintainability issue than an immediate functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration irreversibly DELETEs the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site settings rows after copying them, with no down path that restores them, so the old configuration is permanently destroyed on migration. Operators who need to roll back this deploy lose their configured hosts entirely (down only drops the table); the data migration should preserve the source settings until the feature is confirmed stable.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` performs a destructive `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` after copying values into the new `embeddable_hosts` table, and it is defined with `def change` (no explicit `down` to restore those rows). Rails can reverse `create_table`, but it cannot reverse that raw SQL delete, so rolling back would drop the new table while the old settings remain permanently removed—losing the prior configuration for any rollback to the old code that depends on those settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration crashes with NoMethodError on nil when no site_settings row named 'embed_category' exists, because `execute(...)[0]['id']` indexes into an empty result array before the category_id == 0 fallback is checked. Fresh installs or any database without a seeded embed_category row abort the migration mid-transaction; the null-check is placed after the dereference that can raise.

[ADVISORY] Migrated host strings are interpolated directly into a raw INSERT statement without escaping, so a host value containing a single quote (accepted by the old free-text site setting) breaks or corrupts the migration. Forums whose legacy embeddable_hosts setting contains e.g. `o'brien.example.com` hit a SQL syntax error during deploy; the new model validation would reject such hosts, but the migration runs before any validation can clean them.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` builds a raw SQL INSERT via string interpolation: `VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)` where `h` comes directly from the legacy `site_settings` value split by newlines. There is no quoting/escaping (e.g., `quote`/bind params), so a host containing a single quote would produce invalid SQL or unintended SQL, causing the migration/deploy to fail or corrupt data. This is verifiable from the diff regardless of later model validations, since migration runs before validations apply.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The _hydrateEmbedded change broadens a shared, load-bearing store primitive (singular *_id handling) to also rewrite plural *_ids keys to a pluralized type, a change to core serialization hydration semantics made in service of the embedding feature. Any existing API whose payload coincidentally contains a `*_ids` key now gets those keys deleted and replaced with a hydrated `pluralize(subType)` array; if the subType is not a registered model, _lookupSubType returns undefined and the ids array is silently replaced by [undefined], corrupting consumers of any payload field ending in _ids — this is a silent public-surface change to the store affecting all Ember clients, not just embedding.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `store._hydrateEmbedded` from matching only `*_id` to matching `*_id` and `*_ids` (`/(.+)\_id(s?)$/`), and for the plural case it unconditionally does `obj[k].map(...)`, assigns `obj[self.pluralize(subType)] = hydrated || []`, and deletes the original `*_ids` key. This broadens hydration semantics globally: any payload field ending in `_ids` will be treated as an association list, rewritten, and the original ids array removed. If the subtype isn’t registered or can’t be looked up, the resulting array will contain `undefined` entries (since an array is truthy, `hydrated || []` won’t fall back), and consumers expecting the original `*_ids` field will see it deleted. This is a real, diff-verifiable correctness/backwards-compat risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration string-interpolates former embeddable_hosts setting values directly into INSERT statements. execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)" — a value in the legacy embeddable_hosts site setting containing a single quote breaks out of the string literal and injects arbitrary SQL into the migration run, which executes with full DDL privileges; a malicious or merely quote-containing host value corrupts or drops data during deploy.

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` builds SQL via string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`, where `h` comes from the legacy `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts` split by newlines. If any stored host contains a single quote (or other SQL metacharacters), it will break the SQL string literal and can alter the executed statement, causing migration failure or SQL injection during deploy. The diff shows no escaping/parameterization (e.g., `quote(h)`), so this is a real, diff-grounded defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update and destroy look up EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first and then call methods on the result without checking for nil, producing an unhandled NoMethodError when the id does not exist. A staff user (or any stale admin UI with a deleted host row) submitting a nonexistent id gets a 500 error with a stack trace in production logs instead of a 404, and host.update/destroy never completes — the delete confirmation flow hangs on the client for already-removed hosts.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the code fetches `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately calls `save_host(host)` (which does `host.host = ...`) or `host.destroy` without handling the case where no record exists. If `params[:id]` is invalid/stale, `host` will be `nil` and this will raise `NoMethodError`, resulting in a 500 instead of a 404/handled error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The update action never reads or persists any params, so the admin Embedding page's save action is a silent no-op that still returns a success response. An admin who clicks save on the embedding settings believes changes were saved (200 OK, re-serialized current state) when nothing was written — any future settings added to this UI will silently fail to persist until the action is implemented, and there is currently no server-side code path that writes Embedding-level settings at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that the server-side `Admin::EmbeddingController#update` never reads params or persists anything—it just re-serializes the current `OpenStruct` (`app/controllers/admin/embedding_controller.rb`, `def update`). The Ember controller also defines `saveChanges()` calling `this.get('embedding').update({})` (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6`). However, the provided `embedding.hbs` template does not include any Save button or invoke `saveChanges`, so the claim that “an admin who clicks save on the embedding settings” is not directly verifiable from this diff. Still, exposing a PUT endpoint and a client save action that are effectively no-ops is a concrete, diff-grounded incompleteness/UX risk for future settings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The controller gates mutation of the embed allowlist with ensure_staff rather than requiring an admin, despite every sibling admin controller inheriting AdminController's admin check semantics via routes constrained by AdminConstraint. On any deployment where staff members are not trusted with security settings, a moderator-class user can add an arbitrary host to the embed allowlist (letting their own site embed forum comments and create topics via TopicEmbed.import with cook_method raw_html), broadening the trust boundary the X-Frame-Options/ALLOWALL embed surface depends on.

adjudication.rationale: The new admin endpoints that mutate the embeddable host allowlist are only protected by `ensure_staff` (see `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController` and `Admin::EmbeddingController` `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff`), not an admin-only check. These endpoints are reachable via routes constrained by `AdminConstraint` (`resources :embeddable_hosts` and `get/put customize/embedding`), and the allowlist is now the sole gate for embedding (`EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` now checks `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` and then sets `X-Frame-Options = ALLOWALL`). So any staff user allowed past `AdminConstraint` (commonly includes moderators) could add arbitrary hosts and broaden the embedding trust boundary, which is a security-impacting defect if moderators are not intended to manage this setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The 'find embedded' test asserts fruit 2's colors but the pretender handler for /fruits/:id ignores the requested id and always returns fruits[0] (apple, color_ids [1,2]), so the test validates the mock's wrong-record response, not per-id hydration. The assertion fruitCols.length === 2 passes only because the fixture handler is broken; if the handler were corrected to return fruit 2 (color_ids [3]), this test would fail — meaning the suite currently locks in the broken handler and would mask a real hydration regression for non-first records. Checked: test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6 and test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff: the Pretender route `this.get('/fruits/:id', function() { const fruit = fruits[0]; ... })` always returns `fruits[0]` regardless of `:id` (test/javascripts/helpers/create-pretender.js.es6). Meanwhile the updated `find embedded` test calls `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts `colors` has length 2 with ids `[1,2]` (test/javascripts/models/store-test.js.es6), which matches `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`) not fruit 2 (banana, `color_ids: [3]`). So the test currently passes only because the mock handler is wrong, and would fail if the handler were fixed—meaning the suite is indeed locking in broken per-id behavior and could mask real hydration issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' no longer tests what its name claims: the diff removed the embeddable_hosts presence check from expandable_first_post?, and this test now passes only because embed_truncate defaults to false in that context — the blank-host condition contributes nothing. The behavior change in this diff (expandable_first_post? returning true when no hosts exist but embed_truncate and topic_embed are set) has no test that exercises it; a reader of the suite believes the blank-host guard still exists and a regression restoring/removing the check would go undetected. Checked: spec/models/topic_spec.rb — no test covers the no-hosts-with-truncate-true case.

adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff: `Topic#expandable_first_post?` was changed from `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` to only `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` (app/models/topic.rb). In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb`, the example named `it "is false if embeddable_host is blank"` no longer sets `SiteSetting.embed_truncate = true` or stubs `has_topic_embed?`, so it will pass because the default `embed_truncate` is false and/or `has_topic_embed?` is false—not because any "blank host" guard exists. The suite also lacks a test covering the new behavior where `embed_truncate=true` and `has_topic_embed?=true` but there are no embeddable hosts configured (now via `EmbeddableHost`). This is a test/coverage issue and misleading spec naming, not a directly verifiable production defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The only test for Admin::EmbeddableHostsController asserts the class's superclass — an inheritance check that cannot fail while any controller behavior is broken. create/update/destroy, the category_id-blank fallback to uncategorized_category_id, and render_json_error on validation failure are entirely unverified; a regression in save_host (e.g. nil host from params crashing with NoMethodError) ships green. Checked: this is the only spec file referencing EmbeddableHostsController in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The only test for Admin::EmbeddingController asserts superclass inheritance, so no controller behavior is exercised. The show action's serialization of embedding with embedded host ids and the fetch_embedding ordering (EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)) are unverified; an N+1/ordering/serialization regression ships undetected. Checked: this is the only spec file referencing EmbeddingController in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial behavior in `Admin::EmbeddingController` (`show`/`update` rendering `EmbeddingSerializer` and `fetch_embedding` building an OpenStruct with `EmbeddableHost.all.order(:host)`), but the only added spec `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb` merely asserts the controller inherits from `Admin::AdminController` and does not exercise any action/serialization/ordering behavior. That makes regressions in JSON shape (e.g., `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`) or ordering untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The model spec tests only the trimming happy path of the host format validation; no test exercises a host that fails the regex (e.g. 'not a host', 'eviltrout', empty), so the validation branch is unverifiable from the suite. A loosened or broken regex in EmbeddableHost's validates_format_of (e.g. an edit that accepts any string) passes all specs, letting admins save invalid hosts that then silently fail host_allowed? matching in production embeds. Checked: spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb is the only spec for this model.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new model `EmbeddableHost` with a nontrivial `validates_format_of :host` regex (app/models/embeddable_host.rb), but the new spec file (spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb) only exercises normalization (trimming http/https/paths) and `host_allowed?` with valid-looking hostnames. There is no test asserting that clearly invalid inputs (e.g. empty string, no TLD like 'eviltrout', whitespace like 'not a host') are rejected by the format validation, so a regression that loosens/breaks the regex would not be caught by this suite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration's data-migration logic (site_settings to embeddable_hosts row copying, category_id fallback, SQL string interpolation) has no spec coverage anywhere in the diff. The first row of the execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories INNER JOIN site_settings...") will raise NoMethodError for nil ([]) on any site where embed_category was never set — the [0]['id'].to_i call on an empty result — and this crash-on-migrate path is never exercised, so a fresh install or a site without embed settings blocks on db:migrate. Checked: no spec file in the diff references this migration or EmbeddableHost data migration.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` when looking up the category from the `embed_category` site_setting. If that query returns no rows (e.g., `embed_category` was never set / doesn’t match any category), `[0]` is `nil` and `nil['id']` will raise `NoMethodError`, aborting `db:migrate` before the later fallback logic runs. This crash path is visible directly in the diff, and there’s no test/spec in the diff that exercises the migration logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The data migration guard is a dead guard: `embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0` is always 0 for a SELECT under PostgreSQL, so the INSERT loop never runs while the paired DELETE is unconditional. On any site with existing embeddable_hosts configured, the migration deletes the site_settings rows for embeddable_hosts and embed_category without creating any EmbeddableHost records — every existing embed host is silently lost, embeds stop working, and there is no backup or rollback path.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration reads the old setting via `embeddable_hosts = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'embeddable_hosts'")` and then guards the copy with `embeddable_hosts && embeddable_hosts.cmd_tuples > 0`. For PostgreSQL, `cmd_tuples` is derived from `PQcmdTuples` and for SELECT it typically yields 0, so this condition can be false even when a row is returned. The subsequent `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"` is unconditional, meaning the old configuration can be deleted without any EmbeddableHost rows being inserted, causing loss of existing allowed hosts and breaking embeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The category lookup crashes with NoMethodError when the embed_category site setting row is absent or its value matches no category name. `execute(...)` returns an empty result set, so `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError — the migration aborts mid-run on every site that never set embed_category (the vast majority, since its default is ''), leaving the deploy broken and schema_migrations inconsistent.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration does `execute(...)[0]['id'].to_i` for the embed_category lookup. If the SELECT returns 0 rows (e.g., site never set embed_category or the join finds no matching category), `[0]` is nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run, aborting the migration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true` makes this migration destructive on re-run. If the migration ever re-executes against an environment where the table exists and holds data (restore-from-backup, bin/rake db:migrate against a partially-migrated snapshot), force: true drops the table and destroys all embeddable host rows with no confirmation.

adjudication.rationale: The new migration `20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` creates the table with `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which in Rails will drop and recreate the table if it already exists. If this migration is ever executed against a DB where `embeddable_hosts` already exists (e.g., manual re-run or an environment where the migration isn’t recorded but the table exists), it would destroy existing rows before re-inserting only from old `site_settings`, causing potential data loss.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Host values from the old setting are interpolated directly into the INSERT SQL without escaping or parameterization. Any legacy host value containing a single quote (a user could save e.g. `o'brien.com` via the old host_list setting) breaks the INSERT with a syntax error, aborting the migration before the setting rows are migrated — and the data-integrity layer's validation (the model strips schemes/paths and validates format) is bypassed entirely, so junk rows land in the table unvalidated.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` builds raw SQL with `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', ... )"`, directly interpolating legacy `embeddable_hosts` setting lines (`h`) without escaping/parameterization. A value containing a single quote would produce invalid SQL and abort the migration. It also bypasses the model’s `before_validation` normalization (strip scheme/path) and format validation in `EmbeddableHost`, so any legacy entries with schemes/paths would be inserted verbatim and could later fail matching in `record_for_host` (which compares `lower(host)` to `uri.host`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The migration is irreversible: it DELETEs the embeddable_hosts and embed_category site_settings rows with no down method or export to restore them. Once applied, rolling back discards the original configuration permanently — there is no path to reconstruct the old setting values, so any operator needing to revert this deploy loses their embed configuration.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` uses a `change` method that executes raw SQL to copy values out of `site_settings` and then permanently removes them via `execute "DELETE FROM site_settings WHERE name IN ('embeddable_hosts', 'embed_category')"`. There is no `down` method (or `reversible` block) to restore those deleted `site_settings` rows/values, and Rails also cannot automatically reverse the `execute` statements, making rollback either impossible or unable to reconstruct the prior configuration from the diff alone. This matches the finding about permanent loss of the old settings on revert.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fallback to uncategorized_category_id only covers category_id == 0, but a missing/blank embed_category crashes earlier at the lookup, so the fallback is unreachable in the most common case. Operators who intentionally left embed_category blank (expecting uncategorized posts) hit a failed migration instead of the graceful fallback the code clearly intends.

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` does `execute("SELECT c.id ... WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i`. If the `embed_category` site setting is missing or blank (common if operators relied on default/uncategorized), that query can return zero rows, so `[0]` is `nil` and `['id']` raises before the later `if category_id == 0` fallback can run. Thus the intended fallback to `uncategorized_category_id` is unreachable in that case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] update and destroy call save_host/destroy on a nil host when params[:id] does not match any EmbeddableHost, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 where the admin API contract implies a 404. `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` is nil; `host.host = ...` (line 27) or `host.destroy` (line 19) raises NoMethodError, producing a raw 500 with a stack trace in the admin log instead of a 4xx error payload the frontend's popupAjaxError can render.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`, both `update` and `destroy` fetch the record via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` without handling the not-found case. If no record exists, `host` is `nil`, and `save_host(host)` will call `host.host = ...` / `host.category_id = ...` (in `save_host`) causing a `NoMethodError`. Likewise `destroy` calls `host.destroy` on `nil`. This would yield a 500 instead of a 404-style response.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, the code directly dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]` (new file `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb`, lines in `save_host`). If the request omits the `embeddable_host` envelope (i.e., `params[:embeddable_host]` is `nil`), this will raise `NoMethodError` before any model validation or the `render_json_error(host)` path can run, resulting in a 500. The diff shows no guard/parameter validation to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The delete flow calls destroyRecord().then(...) with no .catch, so a failed DELETE leaves the promise rejection unhandled and the admin gets no error while the row stays in the list with stale state. If the server rejects the destroy (e.g. a 500 or network failure), no popupAjaxError fires, the row remains in the table as if delete silently did nothing, and an unhandled rejection is logged; contrast with save() which does catch popupAjaxError — the delete path has zero error surfacing.

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { ... })` but has no `.catch(...)` (unlike `save()` which `.catch(popupAjaxError)`). If the DELETE request fails/rejects, no error is surfaced and the rejected promise is left unhandled; additionally `deleteHost` is only sent on success so the row remains in the table with no feedback.

The frontend's saveChanges() calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` with no error handling; any admin invocation of the embedding save flow silently no-ops with a 200, leaving the user believing their settings were saved.

So while the endpoint/action is a no-op if invoked, the diff doesn’t prove an actual user-facing broken save flow on this page.
